study.title: Sleep Diary Completion During Routine Insomnia Care
study.background: Earlier research measured diary adherence over 13 nights. Evidence about longer observation during usual insomnia care remains limited.
study.hypothesis: Observed outcomes may change during routine care; this observational study does not establish treatment superiority.

population.study_population: Adults receiving routine care for insomnia.
inclusion_criteria: Adults receiving routine care for insomnia.
exclusion_criteria: Records or planned follow-up information unavailable.

design.study_design: Prospective, single-center observational cohort study of routine care.

arms.name: Routine care cohort
arms.description: Adults receiving routine care for insomnia.

design.intervention_name: Sleep diary review and burden questionnaire

assessments: Sleep diary review and burden questionnaire
procedures.discontinuation: Participants may withdraw at any time.

procedures: Sleep diary review and burden questionnaire
Sleep diary review and burden questionnaire

safety.roles: The investigator assesses and reports safety events.

risks_benefits.risks: Diaries may cause inconvenience and confidentiality risks.
risks_benefits.injury_handling: Research-related concerns will be reported to the investigator.

statistics.analysis_plan: Continuous scores will be summarized using medians and interquartile ranges. Categorical outcomes will be summarized using counts and percentages. No hypothesis tests are planned.

objectives.primary: Describe sleep diary completion during routine insomnia care.

introduction.text: Earlier research measured diary adherence over thirteen nights. Evidence about longer observation during usual insomnia care remains limited.

objectives.text: Characterize how consistently patients record their nightly rest during usual insomnia management.

analysis-plan.methodology.text: Summarize numeric outcomes with the median and interquartile range, and categorical outcomes with frequencies and proportions. The analysis remains descriptive without hypothesis testing.

icf.procedures.text: Study assessments involve sleep diary review and burden questionnaire at Baseline on Day 0, Month 1 on Day 30 with a seven day window, and Month 3 on Day 90 with a seven day window. Eligible adults are 18 to 80 years old. Adults receiving routine care for insomnia. Records or planned follow-up information must be available. You must not have taken part in another study during the ninety days before screening.

prs_objective: Characterize how consistently patients record their nightly rest during usual insomnia management.
